title: Grateful Dead Live at Salt Palace on 1973-02-28

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of a February ’73 show that’s generally clear and well‑balanced, capturing a high‑energy performance highlighted by a stellar The Other One, Eyes of the World and a ripping second set.
ai_review.review: The tapes are a soundboard source with decent clarity – not the sharpest mix in the vault but clean enough to enjoy the band’s tight interplay.  Musically this show is praised for its cohesive first set and an explosive second set featuring The Other One, Eyes of the World, Truckin’/Turn On Your Lovelight, and a soaring Sugar Magnolia finale.  Reviewers repeatedly commend Jerry’s solos and vocals, Phil’s powerful bass intro, and Keith’s standout El Paso work.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (7 of 9 detailed) give 4‑5 stars and highlight exceptional performances, while noting only minor recording imperfections; the strong musical appraisal outweighs the modest soundboard issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Not the sharpest mix in the drawer, but overall decent clarity. Some reviewers mention occasional cuts or a need to lower Phil’s level, yet the tape is clearer than many other Feb ’73 sources.

standout_songs: Truckin' > Turn On Your Lovelight > Eyes > Morning Dew
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set gels quickly and builds momentum, leading into a second‑set marathon that sustains high energy with tight transitions and memorable jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Perfect solo on TLEO, strong lead vocals (Promised Land) and backing harmonies; praised for bluesy scales during Truckin' jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Loud, strong intro to The Other One; solid bass foundation throughout, vocal contributions with Donna, and powerful “bombs” in jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s El Paso highlighted as near‑perfect; overall keyboard work noted as cohesive and supportive.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy (Kreutzmann) praised for tight drumming on El Paso and dynamic fills during Truckin' jam.
